findings.title: db/schema.rb is not updated for the new embeddable_hosts table
findings.body: This migration creates `embeddable_hosts`, but the PR does not update `db/schema.rb`. Discourse's test setup and fresh installs load the schema file, so the new table will be absent from test databases; the new `EmbeddableHost` model, fabricator, and admin endpoints will fail in specs. The migration must be reflected in schema.rb as well.

findings.title: Migration crashes when old site_settings rows are absent
findings.body: The migration assumes `execute(...)[0]` always returns a row for `embed_category` and, on line 15, for `uncategorized_category_id`. In a normal install `embed_category` may have no row at all (defaults live in memory, not necessarily in the table), so `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the upgrade. Use `execute(...).first`/`try` and handle the empty-result case.

findings.title: Old host values are interpolated directly and are not normalized
findings.body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is inserted straight into SQL with string interpolation. A value containing a quote breaks the migration (and is effectively SQL injection from persisted configuration). More importantly, the migration bypasses `EmbeddableHost` normalization, so old entries such as `http://example.com` or `example.com/path` are stored unchanged; `record_for_host` looks up only `URI(host).host` (`example.com`), so those hosts will never match after upgrade and embedding silently stops working.

findings.title: Feed-polled imports lose category after embed_category removal
findings.body: TopicEmbed now derives its category only from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. `SiteSetting.embed_category` has been removed, but TopicEmbed is also used by feed polling, where feed URLs are not necessarily registered as embeddable_hosts. Those imports now pass a nil category and fall into uncategorized, a behavior regression for feed polling. Either keep a fallback setting or require/register feed hosts before removing the global category setting.

findings.title: Nil host causes a 500 instead of a validation error
findings.body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil. The admin controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a request with a missing or nil host raises `NoMethodError` before validation can report an error. This should return a normal validation failure; add a presence check or guard the callback.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts are allowed and can map to different categories
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation on `host` and the migration adds no unique index. The admin UI can therefore create multiple records for the same host with different categories. `record_for_host` uses `.first` without an order, so imported posts can be categorized unpredictably. Add a case-insensitive unique index and model validation.

findings.title: Port is accepted by validation but never matched during lookup
findings.body: The format validator explicitly permits an optional `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against the stored host value. A record stored as `example.com:8080` can therefore never match an embed URL/referer for that host. Either strip the port on save or include the port in the lookup consistently.

findings.title: New hosts saved without a selected category lose their category in the UI
findings.body: For a new host, `categoryId` is null unless the user explicitly chooses a category. The server defaults blank categories to `uncategorized_category_id`, but after save the component overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`, i.e. with null. The row then displays no category and a later edit starts with a blank chooser even though the server stored uncategorized. Use the saved `category_id` from the server response instead of the client-side `categoryId`.

findings.title: New admin controllers only have subclass specs
findings.body: The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert inheritance. There are no request specs for create/update/destroy, authorization, missing host, invalid id, or category defaulting. Those paths contain the nil-host and nil-record failure modes introduced by this controller, so the current tests would not catch them.
